title: CCTV / IP Camera Health Monitoring
exclusions: Does not validate pixel-level tampering, video analytics false-negative rates, or cloud-only consumer cameras outside the enterprise VMS; license-mapped archival tiers and legal hold workflows are out of scope.
evidence: Export the alert result set (camera_id, connection_status, recording_status, storage_util_pct, _time) plus a screenshot or API response JSON from Hikvision ISAPI or the VMS UI for the matching window and store it with the physical security case record.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=physical` sourcetype='nvr:camera_status' where `entity` satisfies `storage_util_pct` > 90 for UC-15.3.11 ('CCTV / IP Camera Health Monitoring'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `physical` / `nvr:camera_status` events where `entity` stays below `storage_util_pct` > 90, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-15.3.11.

dataSources: Poll Hikvision ISAPI device and storage endpoints, Milestone XProtect Management Server REST, Genetec Security Center REST, or ONVIF device-management responses, then land normalized JSON or XML in index=physical as sourcetype="nvr:camera_status" with extracted fields connection_status, recording_status, storage_util_pct, last_frame_time, and camera_id. Use the REST API Modular Input (Splunkbase app ID 1747) or an equivalent Splunk-supported HTTP poller—never embedding credentials in dashboards—to ingest five- to fifteen-minute snapshots aligned with vendor rate limits.
spl:
index=physical sourcetype="nvr:camera_status"
| where connection_status!="online" OR recording_status!="recording" OR storage_util_pct > 90
| table camera_id, location, connection_status, recording_status, storage_util_pct, last_frame_time
| sort connection_status
description: Continuous telemetry from data-center CCTV paths that surfaces camera reachability, active recording arms, NVR-attached disk consumption, and last-frame freshness so operators see coverage loss before an investigation needs footage.
value: Continuous telemetry from data-center CCTV paths that surfaces camera reachability, active recording arms,.... Timely UC-15.3.11 alerting on 'CCTV / IP Camera Health Monitoring' reduces operational risk and delayed incident response before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Deploy REST polling (Splunkbase #1747 modular input or scripted HEC forwarder) against Hikvision ISAPI, Milestone, or Genetec management APIs plus optional ONVIF metadata pulls; normalize into connection_status, recording_status, storage_util_pct, last_frame_time; schedule polls every 5–15 minutes; alert when cameras are not online, recording is paused, or storage_util_pct exceeds ninety percent; trend uptime by zone and reconcile against rack-level physical-access maps.
visualization: Heatmap matrix of zones × camera health, sortable Table of offline channels with storage_util_pct and last_frame_time, radial Gauge for pooled NVR disk headroom, and optional datacenter floor overlay fed from location metadata.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `physical`** — Planned work for 'CCTV / IP Camera Health Monitoring' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `host` remains in-scope for UC-15.3.11. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `nvr:camera_status`** — Scheduled automation elevates `src` without crossing `storage_util_pct` > 90. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `physical` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `nvr:camera_status`** — First 48h baseline for `host` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Confirm network paths from the Splunk heavy forwarder or input tier to each NVR management VLAN; TLS intercept must not break mutual-auth scenarios used by Milestone or Genetec.
• Install REST API Modular Input (Splunkbase app 1747) or maintain an approved custom collector consistent with Custom (NVR API, ONVIF, Hikvision ISAPI); store credentials via Splunk secrets/RBAC—not props.conf literals.
• Map each manufacturer to its documented HTTP surface (Hikvision ISAPI XML/JSON, Milestone REST, Genetec Web SDK) and translate responses into shared keys connection_status, recording_status, storage_util_pct, last_frame_time, camera_id, location.

Configure data collection
• Create modular-input stanzas that GET management URIs every five to fifteen minutes (tighter during commissioning) and stamp _time from the appliance clock inside the payload.
• Route successful polls to index=physical with sourcetype="nvr:camera_status"; optionally duplicate a summary metric stream for executive dashboards.
• For ONVIF complements, call lightweight device-management actions permitted by your VMS and fold identifiers into the same sourcetype via FIELDALIAS so downstream SPL stays unified.

Search, alerting, and access controls
• Base detection SPL on the existing saved pattern targeting index=physical sourcetype="nvr:camera_status"; schedule production alerts with dispatch.earliest_time=-15m when polls run every five minutes to capture two samples minimum.
• Restrict knowledge objects to a dedicated RBAC role such as physical_security_ops plus delegated admins; reviewers without CCTV clearance should see masked location tokens only.

Validate
• Spot-check five cameras per site against the Milestone Smart Client, Genetec Security Desk, or Hikvision web GUI for the identical poll window; reconcile storage_util_pct with NVR RAID dashboards before trusting thresholds.

Operationalize
• Publish a coverage dashboard (status grid + drill-down table), attach webhook or ticketing alert actions, and document escalation when recording_status stays non-recording beyond vendor SLA timers.
